original_question: For a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism on a closed symplectic manifold, is it true that either the number of periodic orbits is finite or the number P(T) of primitive periodic orbits of period at most T grows at least quadratically, in the sense that lim inf_{T -> +infinity} log P(T) / log T >= 2?
target_in_paper: Problem 1 in the unnumbered contribution by Bernhard Albach, Umberto Hryniewicz, and Alexandru Oancea, with its counting convention inherited from the immediately preceding discussion of Conjecture 1 for Reeb flows. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2602.12896))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s actual target almost verbatim: it asks about Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms of closed symplectic manifolds, keeps the finite-versus-quadratic-growth dichotomy, and correctly phrases the growth lower bound using a liminf of logarithmic growth. It also correctly avoids importing the Reeb-flow-specific exception “exactly two periodic orbits,” which belongs to Conjecture 1 and not to Problem 1. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2602.12896))
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, the question should define a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism as the time-one map of a Hamiltonian isotopy on a closed symplectic manifold (M,ω); the paper states only “Hamiltonian diffeomorphism on a closed symplectic manifold” and leaves this standard meaning implicit. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2602.12896))

The counting function should be defined explicitly. The nearby context says that one counts only primitive periodic orbits and does not count multiply covered or iterated ones; Problem 1 then uses this convention without reintroducing notation. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2602.12896))

For a diffeomorphism, “period at most T” should be clarified as “least period n∈ℕ with n≤T,” since the problem concerns discrete-time dynamics even though the paper writes the growth condition using a real parameter T. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2602.12896))

If the notation P(T) is used, it should be declared explicitly, because the paper states the growth condition but does not introduce the symbol P(T) in the visible prose of Problem 1. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2602.12896))

It should also be made explicit that Problem 1 is asked with no extra assumptions such as asphericity, monotonicity, nondegeneracy, or a dimension restriction; the authors mention standard symplectic tori, aspherical manifolds, and CP^n only later as test cases in Problems 2 and 3, not as part of the main problem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2602.12896))
refined_question: Let (M,ω) be a closed (compact, without boundary) symplectic manifold, and let φ∈Ham(M,ω) be a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism, i.e. the time-one map of a Hamiltonian isotopy. For T>0, let P(T) denote the number of primitive periodic orbits of φ whose least period n∈ℕ satisfies n≤T, where each periodic orbit is counted once at its least period (so iterates are not counted separately). Must the following dichotomy hold: either φ has only finitely many periodic orbits, or liminf_{T→∞} (log P(T))/(log T) ≥ 2?
justification: The draft is aiming at Problem 1, not at the Reeb-flow Conjecture 1 itself. The paper first recalls Conjecture 1 for Reeb flows and its counting convention—count primitive periodic orbits up to period T—and then says explicitly that the confirmed Reeb-flow case is not the proposed problem; instead, the authors ask whether the same phenomenon should hold “in any dimension” for Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms of closed symplectic manifolds. Problems 2 and 3 are presented only as particular test cases, so they should not replace or be folded into the main question. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2602.12896))
